children: Basis bids for corn and soybeans shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast eased on Tuesday, as grain futures rallied after the US Department of Agriculture forecast the US harvest and stocks below trade expectations, traders said.

US soybean futures surged on Tuesday after USDA raised its US harvest outlook by less than expected in a monthly report and projected tighter supplies in the year ahead. Corn futures also rallied as the USDA cut its US production and stocks forecasts by more than expected.
Some exporters have been turning to Brazil for sourcing soybeans, as supplies there have become cheaper than sourcing in the US, said Rich Nelson, chief commodity analyst at Allendale Inc.

The US Department of Agriculture confirmed private sales of 312,700 metric tons of US corn and 150,000 tons of US soybeans to Mexico for delivery in the 2026/27 marketing year that began on September 1.
Forecasts for rain showers across parts of Illinois and Indiana on Wednesday could slow harvest for a day or two, market analysts said, but such potential delays are expected to be short-lived.
At the Gulf, CIF corn barges loaded in November were bid at 92 cents over Chicago Board of Trade December (CZ26) futures, down 1 cent from Monday.
Meanwhile, CIF corn barges loaded in November traded at 94 cents over December futures, and December loadings traded at 101 cents over futures.
FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in December eased 1 cent at around 109 cents over futures.
For soybeans, CIF barges loaded in November were bid at 104 cents over CBOT January soybean (SF27) futures, down 2 cents from Monday.
CIF soybean barges loaded in January 2027 traded at 114 cents over January futures, while split-January loadings traded at 116 cents over futures.
FOB export premiums for Gulf soybeans loaded in December eased 1 cent, at about 117 cents over January futures.
